answer: PoA binds each identity’s bonded collateral to its signed actions, so splitting control across k identities does not dilute accountability: correlated equivocation triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k², including cross-identity evidence. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the coordinated swarm, making added sybils increase exposure rather than safety. Like yarrow stalks on a ridge watched by a sparrow, identities remain separately counted, but linked proofs can reveal common coordination.
